# FDG9111

> DO mark generic type parameters on generic delegates as contravariant when the type parameter is used as input, but not output, and your language supports creating contravariant types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.8.1 Contravariance.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9111
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Mark the type parameter '{0}' of the delegate '{1}' as contravariant (in); it is only used as input

Library only: the reason given (in the FDG9112 body, which covers both) is that changing a released delegate is a breaking change, so the variance is declared up front. The text has no body of its own. FDG9111 reports an invariant type parameter of an externally visible generic delegate that appears only in input positions of its signature, as the compiler does, with one exception: parameters passed by value, property setters and event types are input positions; return types, property getters and base interfaces are output positions; ref, out and in parameters, ref returns and, more strictly than the compiler, constraints of the type's own type parameters are both; constraints of method type parameters are inputs; and in a generic type argument the position is kept for a covariant type parameter, flipped for a contravariant one and both for an invariant one. A type parameter that is not used at all could take either modifier and is not reported, and neither is one that a static member uses, so coverage is partial. Adding the modifier changes the declaration of a public type and can make existing conversions and overload resolutions ambiguous, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
